actions.why: Two structured-data problems on the SoftwareApplication node "Battery Sensei": (1) it has neither aggregateRating nor review — only add one if the site has real ratings or reviews from its own users, and then also display that rating on the page; never take a rating from an app store or another site, and do not invent one if none exists. (2) The markup names the offer price 6.99 USD, but the rendered page shows 9.99 where the raw text shows 6.99. The owner decides which price the offer states: update the offer's price in the JSON-LD so it matches the price the page actually shows after it loads (currently $9.99 for Lifetime), and make sure the price in the markup is the one visitors see. Do not add the price to the page as static text to quiet the check — the markup must agree with what the page displays.
actions.title: Fix the structured data: show a genuine rating and match the markup price to the page
actions.expectedEffect: The markup will describe what visitors actually see: a price that matches the on-page offer, and — if genuine user ratings exist and are shown — a rating consistent with the page. This keeps the structured data aligned with the visible page as Google asks.

actions.why: https://battery-sensei.app/ currently answers with a 307 (temporary) redirect to https://www.battery-sensei.app/. A redirect to another host should use 301 or 308 so search engines consolidate signals to the www URL instead of treating the hop as temporary. Configure the server or host to return a 301 (or 308) for this redirect. The ranking data in this audit comes from the www URL, which is the same page after the redirect, so it applies here.
actions.title: Make the battery-sensei.app → www redirect permanent
actions.expectedEffect: A permanent redirect tells crawlers the www host is the canonical home, so link signals are not diluted across the two hostnames. The page content itself does not change.

actions.why: The site has German, Spanish, French and Japanese versions (https://www.battery-sensei.app/de, /es, /fr, /ja), but the rendered page contains no <a> links to any of them. The language switcher (EN DE ES FR 日) appears not to be real anchor links the crawler can follow. Add visible <a> elements to each language version — for example in the existing language menu and/or the footer — so visitors and crawlers can reach them.
actions.title: Link the other language versions from the page
actions.expectedEffect: Visitors can switch languages, and crawlers can discover the other language versions from the English page, which supports the localized pages being indexed.

actions.why: The goal's action is to buy, but neither the mobile nor the desktop first screen shows a buy link or button; the only purchase controls ("Get Lifetime", "Become a patron") sit far down the page near the pricing section. Add a buy control to the first screen — for example a "Get Lifetime — $9.99" button (the price the page states for Lifetime) beside or under the hero's existing "Download for macOS" call to action, and keep it visible on mobile and desktop.
actions.title: Put a buy control on the first screen
actions.expectedEffect: Visitors who arrive ready to buy can start the purchase from the top of the page instead of scrolling to pricing; the existing checkout flow stays unchanged.

actions.why: This page takes payment (it sells Lifetime and Yearly Patron licenses), and it already links contact info (mailto:info@battery-sensei.app), but there is no link to payment information and none to returns or exchange/refund information. Add short links in the footer (or near the pricing cards) to a payments page (acceptable payment methods) and to the refund/returns terms — the FAQ already covers "Can I get a refund?", so a link to that answer or a dedicated legal/refund page works.
actions.title: Add payment and returns links to the page
actions.expectedEffect: Buyers can find how they can pay and how refunds work before purchasing, which supports trust at the point of sale and satisfies the page's obligations as a payment-taking page.
